response: Cycloplegic autorefraction is not mandatory for all young adults, but it is recommended for young hypermetropic adults who are experiencing symptoms of asthenopia. This is because young hypermetropic adults may possess latent hypermetropia, which can be detected through cycloplegic refraction. In contrast, young myopic adults may exhibit pseudomyopia, but the degree is typically mild, around -0.5 D. Therefore, cycloplegic refraction should be performed in young hypermetropic adults complaining of various signs of asthenopia to accurately assess their refractive error.
